newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh eyes higher growth in 1997/98.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh eyes higher growth in 1997/98.

text.p: The main focus of Bangladesh's 1997/98 (July-June) Annual Development Plan is to raise growth of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) to at least six percent from the current 5.7 percent, State Minister of Planning Mohiuddin Khan Alamgir said on Thursday.

Alamgir said the plan, approved on Wednesday by the National Economic Council headed by Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, also aimed to expedite efforts to reduce poverty and improve literacy as part of human resources development.
Over half of Bangladesh's 120 million people live below the poverty line and only 30 percent can read and write, according to official figures.
Before taking effect on July 1, the plan, known by the acronym ADP, needs formal approval by parliament, which begins its budget session on Tuesday.
Total funding outlay in the ADP would be 130 billion taka ($3.02 billion), which is more than 10 billion taka ($230 million) higher than the 1996/97 ADP, the minister said.

"Besides raising the GDP and alleviation of poverty, overall development of social sectors including agriculture, water supply, infrastructures, investments, education and standard of living of the common people are among top priorities in the next ADP," he told Reuters
Alamgir said some 48 percent of the ADP fundings would come from domestic resources and the rest from overseas donors as project aid.

In the 1997/98 ADP, the highest allocation of about 17 billion taka ($390 million) will be for education, followed by industry 12.3 billion taka ($280) and transportation about 12 billion taka ($270 million). "Agriculture is our mainstay in the economy. It's contribution to the GDP is about 35 percent and 80 percent of our people depends on agriculture," he said.
"But we need more expenditure in other sectors than agriculture," he added.
